A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GreedTok partition-cover research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original compression, language-model pretraining and approximation experiments in Section 5, plus token-set analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains the original compression, language-model pretraining and approximation results in Section 5 and token-set analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: GreedTok's greedy selection, coverage constraints, token ordering and encoding procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–4. Section 6 discusses possible future adaptations without incorporating them into the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain UN, arXiv, Wikipedia and PubMed compression evaluation, RefinedWeb approximation experiments, DCLM pretraining and the same downstream benchmarks. No additional dataset, language or task scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: BPE and Unigram remain the compression and token-set comparators, GreedWMC remains the approximation reference, and BPE remains the pretraining baseline. Newly discussed extension methods are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Vocabulary budgets, model architecture, training iterations and token counts, dataset proportions, benchmark splits and evaluation metrics are retained. Pretraining settings move from v2 Section 5.2 to v3 Appendix F.2; abbreviated dataset statistics do not establish changed settings.

E4.justification: The approximation analyses in Figures 3–4 and token-overlap, whole-word and likelihood analyses in Figures 5–6 and Table 8 are retained. Moving Appendix B to Appendix E introduces no new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: V3 Checklist item 7 newly discloses that language-model variants were not repeatedly trained because of cost and explains the lack of statistical significance reporting. This clarifies existing practice; Figure 4 retains the same 40 independent RefinedWeb runs.

E6.justification: Compression, benchmark and likelihood scores and all plotted data are retained. However, Section 5.2 changes the reported equal-text finding from GreedTok being ahead to performing comparably to BPE at equivalent byte lengths, revising the qualitative finding associated with unchanged Figure 2b.

T1.justification: The NP-hardness proof, non-submodularity and non-supermodularity examples, MIP/WMC derivations, Unigram relation and worst-case runtime arguments are retained. Their relocation and the expanded empirical explanation of lazy updates do not introduce a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, five contribution statements and central conclusion retain the same claims about the partition-cover formulation, NP-hardness, greedy tokenizer, compression and pretraining benefits, and empirical approximation behavior.

C2.justification: V3 adds explicit limitations concerning BPE-only pretraining comparisons, 1B model scale and absent low-resource language evaluation, and qualifies lazy-runtime scaling as empirical. It removes v2's explanation of the unequal GTEP/BPEM dataset proportions, although those proportions remain tabulated.

D1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds implementation guidance about small batches of lazy score updates. Most pretraining details are relocated unchanged, but the direct DCLM dataset access link present in v2 is removed. The implementation repository link remains available in the PDF.

R1.justification: The new Future extensions discussion adds BPE-Dropout, PickyBPE, BoundlessBPE, SuperBPE and VOLT, and expands discussion of PathPiece compatibility. This locally broadens research positioning while retaining the principal novelty comparisons.

P1.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes the narrative: Section 4 is condensed, detailed non-modularity and MIP/WMC material moves into Appendices A–C, and pretraining details move to Appendix F.2. It also adds Future extensions, Limitations and the conference checklist.

P2.justification: V3 adopts NeurIPS typography and layout and extensively relocates and reformats displays. V2 Table 1 becomes appendix Table 5, dataset statistics become a compact wrapped table, and figures and algorithm blocks are redistributed. The embedded plots themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 better calibrates the unchanged evidence through explicit scale, language and replication limitations and more cautious equal-text and runtime interpretations. Removing the dataset link and explanation of unequal GTEP/BPEM proportions modestly reduces accessibility and clarity, although the proportions remain tabulated. Overall, the transparency gains support a limited improvement.
